title: Cross-slice p95/p99 benchmarking harness and interactive explorer for endpoints, models, and regions
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable benchmarking and regression-detection pipeline that computes p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec baselines, slices by endpoint, model version, and region, and exposes an interactive explorer + alerting rules for regressions.

Context: We currently have macro percentiles and route-level dashboards, but lack a single synthetic load harness + sliceable analytics explorer that ties a benchmark run to a baseline, explains variance across model/region combinations, and triggers actionable alerts when p95/p99 regresses beyond configurable thresholds. This ticket implements the harness, the aggregation schema, a Grafana-like explorer, and a regression watcher that posts findings into Linear and Slack.

Success criteria / acceptance:
- Synthetic harness that can replay production request traces and generate tokens/sec and latency histograms at configurable concurrency and seq lengths.
- Aggregation pipeline that produces per-run p50/p90/p95/p99 and tokens/sec broken down by endpoint, model_version, and region.
- Explorer UI where SRE/PM/Eng can select any combination of endpoint/model/region and see baseline vs run overlay, plus heatmap of slice deltas.
- Regression watcher that detects >10% p95 or >15% p99 degradation relative to baseline with false-positive suppression for low-volume slices (min 100 samples).
- On-detect workflow: create a prefixed Linear issue, attach run metadata and top contributing slices, and post to #infra-quantiles with playbook links.

Out of scope: automatic rollback of model variants, automatic capacity allocation changes (will be another ticket).
comments: 2026-02-19: Kickoff — agreed to reuse existing request-replay infra but add tokenization-aware replay so tokens/sec metrics are accurate. Assigned to Liam.

2026-02-24: Prototyped harness that replays traces with variable sequence length bucketing. Early results show tokens/sec stable but p99 sensitive to concurrency spikes. Added adaptive warmup to mitigate cold-KV-cache artifacts.
2026-03-02: Design feedback from PM (Evelyn Park): explorer should surface both absolute and relative regressions and let users pin a baseline run. UX mock draft linked in attachments.
2026-03-05: Engineering review — we decided to persist per-request KV-cache hit flags to help explain regressions caused by cache churn vs model slowdown.

2026-03-10: Performance experiments (run id RB-2026-0310-01) attached. Noted a 12% p95 increase for model-x86-1 at region eu-west under synthetic high-burst load with concurrency 48. Created follow-up investigation ENG-10033.
2026-03-12: PR opened for aggregation pipeline and explorer API. Requesting review from Data Infra (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1227).
2026-03-14: Regression watcher rule tuned to exclude slices with <100 requests and to require persistent degradation for 3 consecutive runs before firing an alert.
